question.text: Under SEBI Circular dated October 21, 2021, the Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) of a Category III AIF shall be filed with SEBI:

answer.text: Directly by the Sponsor — no intermediary required.
Through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker who issues a due-diligence certificate.
Through the Custodian for safekeeping purposes.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** As per SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I/DF6/P/CIR/2021/645 dated October 21, 2021, the PPM must be filed with SEBI through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker at the time of seeking registration or launching new schemes. The merchant banker conducts independent due diligence on disclosures and provides a due-diligence certificate. Intimations of specific PPM term changes (per SEBI Circular April 29, 2024) may be filed directly without merchant banker involvement. **The Trap:** Option A ignores the merchant-banker requirement. Option B confuses trustee duties with PPM filing. Option D swaps custodian and merchant banker roles. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C and XIX-D test the same merchant-banker filing rule. XIX-B (distributor) uses the PPM as key disclosure evidence. X-B (IA L2) references the PPM as pre-investment disclosure. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Budget 6-10 weeks for merchant-banker due diligence. The DD certificate requires audited track record of IM, KYC of sponsor, strategy-risk mapping, and fee-disclosure completeness. Start merchant-banker onboarding at the same time as drafting PPM v1, not after — MB sign-off is the critical path item pre-launch.
